## How I approached it

I loaded the `wcag-audit-patterns` skill for the severity taxonomy (Critical = blockers, Serious = significant barrier for a user group, Moderate = quality/robustness degradation), then read `page.html` and its details reference. Since no browser/axe tooling was available in the sandbox, I verified the structural facts programmatically with a throwaway Node script (removed afterward) rather than eyeballing the markup — confirming `<html lang="en">`, one `<h1>`, an *empty* `<head>`, and a clickable `<div>` with zero `tabindex`/`role`/`aria-*` attributes.

## Findings

**Critical (1)**
- `<div onclick="buy()">` is not keyboard accessible — the page's only control is unreachable by keyboard and unannounced to screen readers (2.1.1). Blocks purchase, the primary action.

**Serious (2)**
- Missing `<title>` — empty `<head>`, so the page is unidentifiable in tabs and screen-reader announcements (2.4.2).
- Custom widget with no name, role, or value — reported as static text with no semantics (4.1.2).

**Moderate (1)**
- No landmarks — no `<main>`/regions, so users can't jump to primary content (1.3.1).

## Two judgment calls worth flagging

- **I deliberately did *not* report a missing skip link.** 2.4.1 requires bypass blocks only when repeated content precedes the main content; this page has no navigation, so there is nothing to bypass. It's a common over-report on tiny pages.
- **The `<html lang="en">` is correct**, so 3.1.1 passes — I recorded it under "checked and not reported" along with the non-applicable checks (contrast, labels, media) to make the negative results auditable rather than silently omitted.

I also noted the missing `<!DOCTYPE html>` and `<meta charset>` as best-practice items only, since 4.1.1 Parsing is obsolete in WCAG 2.2. The single highest-leverage fix is swapping the `<div onclick>` for a native `<button>`, which clears the Critical finding and one Serious one simultaneously.

## What was wrong and how I fixed it

I first consulted the `wcag-audit-patterns` skill (which explicitly directs to "native HTML first" rather than ARIA patches), read `check.sh`/`check.js`/`a11y-rules.js` to see which rules are enforced, and reproduced the failures:

```
violation: input-missing-label
violation: div-onclick
```

**1. `input-missing-label` → SC 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions (Level A)**
The text input had no associated label. I used the skill's preferred remediation (Option 1, a *visible* `<label>` wired with `for`/`id`) rather than an `aria-label`, so the field is labelled for sighted users and assistive tech alike:
```html
<label for="name">Full name</label>
<input id="name" type="text" name="name">
```

**2. `div-onclick` → SC 2.1.1 Keyboard / 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A)**
A `<div onclick>` is not focusable, has no role, and cannot be activated by keyboard or announced as a control. Instead of the skill's ARIA-`role="button"` workaround (which only silences the linter and still leaves it non-keyboard-operable), I replaced it with a native semantic element inside the form:
```html
<button type="submit">Submit</button>
```
This removes the `onclick` handler entirely and is focusable, keyboard-operable, and correctly named "Submit" — the smallest change that is *actually* correct, not just checker-clean.

## Verification

- `bash check.sh` → `page passes the accessibility contract checks`, exit 0
- Direct rule-set run returns `violations: []` — all nine rules satisfied (lang, title, h1, images, tables, links, plus the two above)

## One thing to flag for you

The checker is deliberately narrow — it reports only violations, and passing it is not the same as being accessible. Two residual issues sit **outside** its scope and would still be caught by a real audit (e.g. axe-core):

- **No `submitForm()` definition** — the old div referenced a function that doesn't exist. The native button fixes the semantics, but the form still needs a real `action`/handler to do anything.
- **No error handling** — for a sign-up form, SC 3.3.1/3.3.3 (error identification and suggestion) will apply once validation is added; this fixture has none, so it's not currently a violation.

I left both alone since they're out of scope for this contract, but they're worth addressing before this page ships.
